operations.name: allowance.get
operations.description: How many uses a pass, membership or other allowance holder has spent and has left, in the period containing `at` (default now): this week or month (from Monday, or the 1st, in its time zone), or in all for a pass of N. Staff also get its uses per period (null is unlimited), whether it can be spent (live), and the dates it is valid between; a signed-in customer reads their own only, with the terms their own record shows them. Anyone else's is not found. Read-only: uses are spent by booking.

object.description: An extension object that holds an allowance

at.description: The time to read the period of (a class's start), ISO 8601; default now

uses.description: Uses per period; null is unlimited. Left out when the caller may not read it

zone.description: The time zone weeks and months are counted in

validUntil.description: A spender's time must be before this

live.description: Its state lets it be spent (not paused, used up, ended or void)

at.description: The time the period was read for

key.description: total, week:<Monday's local date> or month:<YYYY-MM>

left.description: Uses that can still be spent in it; 0 when the holder cannot pay then, null when unlimited

operations.name: capacity.get
operations.description: How many places a record of an object with a capacity has left (a ticket type, a class). Staff get places, held (while someone pays), taken (paid), available, and the pool's numbers when the record draws on a parent's places. Customers and the public get only what the object shows: the number left, a low-stock warning, or available / sold out. Read-only; claims nothing.

object.description: An extension object that declares a capacity

status.description: `low` only when the object shows a low-stock warning and few are left

available.description: Places left; null when unlimited. Shown to outsiders only when `show` allows

operations.name: content.get
operations.description: Read one published record of a content object (a blog post) by its slug, as the public reads it: its published version, with only the fields the object lets the public read. An old slug of a record whose slug changed answers `redirect` with the slug it has now. A draft, an unpublished record and an unknown slug are all not found. Read-only.

object.description: A publishable object the public reads, e.g. `content.post`

slug.description: Where the record is now: read it by this slug

operations.name: content.list
operations.description: A page of the published records of a content object (blog posts), as the public reads them: published versions only, with only the fields the object lets the public read. Newest first by default (the object's date, else when each was published). Filter and sort on those fields; pass nextCursor back as cursor. Read-only.

object.description: A publishable object the public reads, e.g. `content.post`

operations.name: content.preview
operations.description: Read the working copy of one record of a content object with a preview link's token: what staff are editing, before it is published, with only the fields the public would read. The token names one record and works until it expires; for any other record, or after, it is not found. Read-only.

object.description: A publishable object the public reads, e.g. `content.post`

token.description: The token of a preview link

operations.name: me.deleteAccount
operations.description: Delete your customer account and ask for your personal data to be erased. You are signed out everywhere at once and can no longer sign in. Staff then erase your data, or tell you by email why some of it must be kept, by the due date returned. Asking again changes nothing.

operations.name: me.get
operations.description: Your own Person, as a signed-in customer: your name, primary email and primary phone, and your account's sign-in address (signInEmail, the one the emailed code verified, with signInEmailVerified). Link records kept elsewhere to a customer by signInEmail only: primaryEmail is a contact address staff can change. Read-only.

signInEmail.description: The address you sign in with: the one the emailed code verified, lower-cased. Not the Person's contact email (primaryEmail), which staff can change. The only address to trust when linking records kept elsewhere to this customer.

signInEmailVerified.description: Whether signInEmail was verified by an emailed code. True for every signed-in customer.

operations.name: me.sessions.list
operations.description: The places you are signed in, as a signed-in customer: each session's id, whether it is a browser or an app on a device (with the device's name), when it began, when it was last used and when it expires, and which one is this one. Read-only.

operations.name: me.sessions.revoke
operations.description: Sign out one of your sessions, as a signed-in customer, by its id from me.sessions.list. A session that is not yours is not found.

operations.name: me.signOut
operations.description: Sign out of this session, as a signed-in customer. Your other sessions stay signed in (end them with me.sessions.revoke).

operations.name: me.update
operations.description: Change your own name or primary phone, as a signed-in customer. Only the fields you pass change; pass null to clear one. Your email cannot be changed here. Returns your Person.

operations.name: media.play
operations.description: A short-lived token to play one ready video, and where it plays (HLS, DASH, Stream's player), signed by the host: staff may play any; a customer or the public only a video that a published record they may read shows, in a part they may read (a lesson's video only for a holder of access to its course, a trailer for anyone). Anything else, and a made-up id, is not found. The token is for this video only, lives at most an hour, and never allows a download. Read-only.

record.description: The record that shows it, to look only there

field.description: The field of that record that shows it

purpose.description: stream: to watch. (A download for offline viewing is not offered yet.)

seconds.description: How long the token lives; at most, and by default, an hour

poster.description: The poster frame Stream made, with the token

operations.name: media.serve
operations.description: Whether the caller may be served one picture or downloadable file, and at what width: staff any live one; a customer or the public only one that a published record they may read shows in a part they may read. Anything else is not found, and so is a video (it plays with media.play). The media route (`/api/media/<id>`) streams it. Read-only.

width.description: The width to serve; null for the original

public.description: Served because published content shows it

operations.name: my.get
operations.description: One of your own records (or one that a record of yours points to, such as your ticket's event), as a signed-in customer, with only the fields you may see. A record that is not yours is not found. Read-only.

object.description: The object, e.g. `person` or an extension object such as `shop.order`

currency.description: For an object that is for sale: the currency every price of it is in (the deployment's one currency), or null until one is set. Absent for any other object.

operations.name: my.list
operations.description: A page of your own records of an object, as a signed-in customer (and the records every signed-in customer may read, where the object shares some, and the ones a record of yours points to, such as your ticket's event): only the records that are yours and only the fields you may see. Filter and sort on those fields; pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page. Read-only.

object.description: The object, e.g. `person` or an extension object such as `shop.order`

currency.description: For an object that is for sale: the currency every price of it is in (the deployment's one currency), or null until one is set. Absent for any other object.

operations.name: order.cancel
operations.description: Cancel an order. A signed-in customer can cancel their own order while nothing has been paid on it. Staff can also cancel an order that is part paid (a deposit was paid): that gives up its places, and refunding what was paid is a separate step. A paid order is refunded, not cancelled. Returns the order.

refunded.description: What has gone back to the buyer, confirmed by the provider

taxAmount.description: The tax inside what has been paid, as the payment provider calculated it. Prices include it, so it does not add to the total. Zero when tax is off or none was charged.

taxRefunded.description: The tax the provider said went back with refunds

taxCountry.description: The country the latest taxed payment was for

taxAmount.description: The tax inside this line's payments, as the payment provider calculated it

operations.name: order.checkout
operations.description: Open the payment provider's own page to pay for an order, and get its address to send the buyer to. The host says what is charged: the whole price or the deposit for an order with nothing paid (no amount may be given), or, for a part-paid order, the balance or a part of it of at least the set minimum (`amount`, in the currency's minor unit). The buyer comes back to `returnUrl`, which must be on one of the deployment's listed sites; coming back does not mark anything paid. Only the provider's confirmation does. A guest passes the order's token; a signed-in customer pays their own orders.

token.description: A guest's token for the order

returnUrl.description: Where the buyer comes back to

amount.description: Part-paid orders only: how much to pay towards the balance, in minor units

operations.name: order.get
operations.description: Get one order with its lines: its state, amounts (in the currency's minor unit), what has been paid, the balance and when it is due. A signed-in customer gets their own orders only; anyone else's is not found. Read-only.

refunded.description: What has gone back to the buyer, confirmed by the provider

taxAmount.description: The tax inside what has been paid, as the payment provider calculated it. Prices include it, so it does not add to the total. Zero when tax is off or none was charged.

taxRefunded.description: The tax the provider said went back with refunds

taxCountry.description: The country the latest taxed payment was for

taxAmount.description: The tax inside this line's payments, as the payment provider calculated it

operations.name: order.start
operations.description: Start an order for one or more records that are for sale, as a signed-in customer, a guest (with an email address) or staff. The host prices it from the records: a caller never sends a price or a total. The order starts pending and is not paid: paying happens on the payment provider's page (order.checkout), and only the provider's confirmation marks it paid. An unpaid order expires after a few minutes. Returns the order with its lines and amounts in the currency's minor unit; a guest also gets `token`, shown once, which is the only way back to the order (order.view).

object.description: The object of the record to buy

lines.description: What to buy. There is no price here: the host reads it from each record, and a price or total sent anyway is ignored.

pay.description: full: pay the whole price now. deposit: pay the deposit now and the balance by its due date, when every line offers a deposit.

email.description: The buyer's email address. Required when the caller is not a signed-in customer; a signed-in customer's order uses their account's address and must not pass one.

refunded.description: What has gone back to the buyer, confirmed by the provider

taxAmount.description: The tax inside what has been paid, as the payment provider calculated it. Prices include it, so it does not add to the total. Zero when tax is off or none was charged.

taxRefunded.description: The tax the provider said went back with refunds

taxCountry.description: The country the latest taxed payment was for

taxAmount.description: The tax inside this line's payments, as the payment provider calculated it

token.description: A guest's key to this order. Null for everyone else.

operations.name: order.view
operations.description: See one order with the token it was started with (a guest's link from order.start or the confirmation email). The token opens that order only, while it is open and for 30 days after it closes. A wrong id, a wrong token and an old link are all not found. Read-only.

refunded.description: What has gone back to the buyer, confirmed by the provider

taxAmount.description: The tax inside what has been paid, as the payment provider calculated it. Prices include it, so it does not add to the total. Zero when tax is off or none was charged.

taxRefunded.description: The tax the provider said went back with refunds

taxCountry.description: The country the latest taxed payment was for

taxAmount.description: The tax inside this line's payments, as the payment provider calculated it

operations.name: subscription.cancel
operations.description: End a subscription when its current paid period (or trial) ends: nothing more is charged, and what it gives lasts until then. A signed-in customer cancels their own; staff any, with the subscriptions:manage permission. Nothing is refunded (a period's refund is order.refund). It can be undone until the period ends (subscription.resume). Asked of the payment provider: the subscription shows it once the provider confirms. Staff can instead end it at once (`now: true`): nothing more is charged, nothing is refunded and what it gives stops when the provider confirms; a customer cannot. A person decides, not an AI assistant.

now.description: Staff only: end it now instead of when its period ends

requested.description: Asked of the provider; the subscription shows it once the provider confirms

operations.name: subscription.get
operations.description: Get one subscription: its plan, price per period, state (trial, active, past due, ended…), the current period and whether it ends when that period does. A signed-in customer gets the subscriptions they pay for only; anyone else's is not found. Read-only.

amount.description: The price of one period, in the currency's minor unit, tax included

currentPeriodEnd.description: When the current paid period (or trial) ends: the next charge

cancelAtPeriodEnd.description: Set to end when the current period ends

cancelAt.description: A date it is set to end on at the provider (its dashboard), or null

actionUrl.description: The provider's page to confirm a renewal on, while one waits

operations.name: subscription.list
operations.description: A page of subscriptions, newest first unless sorted otherwise. Filter on state, planObject, planId, payerPersonId, holderPersonId, cancelAtPeriodEnd, currentPeriodEnd, failingSince. A signed-in customer sees the ones they pay for only. Pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page. Read-only.

amount.description: The price of one period, in the currency's minor unit, tax included

currentPeriodEnd.description: When the current paid period (or trial) ends: the next charge

cancelAtPeriodEnd.description: Set to end when the current period ends

cancelAt.description: A date it is set to end on at the provider (its dashboard), or null

actionUrl.description: The provider's page to confirm a renewal on, while one waits

operations.name: subscription.offer.mine
operations.description: The signed-in customer's own continuation offers they can still take: a plan, free until the date they have paid up to on another platform, then charged. Take one with subscription.start { offerId }. chargedNow: under 48 hours are left, so taking it now is charged at once. askUs: its plan is no longer on sale and there is no single other to follow to; the member asks the company. Read-only.

askUs.description: No plan on sale to take it on: ask the company (it has been told)

operations.name: subscription.portal
operations.description: Open the payment provider's customer portal for the signed-in customer: the card they pay with, their billing details and past invoices. Cancelling and plan changes are not there (subscription.cancel). The address is short-lived and opens in its own page, never a frame.

returnUrl.description: Where the portal's back link goes

operations.name: subscription.resume
operations.description: Keep a subscription going that was set to end when its period does, before that happens: the provider charges the next period as usual. A signed-in customer resumes their own; staff any, with the subscriptions:manage permission. An end date set at the provider another way is refused: staff change it there. Asked of the payment provider: the subscription shows it once the provider confirms. A person decides, not an AI assistant.

requested.description: Asked of the provider; the subscription shows it once the provider confirms

operations.name: subscription.start
operations.description: Start a subscription to a plan (a record of an object sold every week, month or year), as a signed-in customer, a guest (with an email address) or staff for someone. Opens the payment provider's own page, which takes the card; the provider charges each period on its own schedule, after the plan's free trial when it has one. A trial is one per person per plan, and only for a signed-in customer (or staff with subscriptions:manage starting it for a person): a guest is charged from the start, and `noTrial` says why no trial was given. Starting again while the page you opened with a trial is still open gives that page. A signed-in customer with a continuation offer (moving their subscription from another platform) takes it with `offerId`: free until their paid-up date, then charged, with no trial on top; with under 48 hours left it is charged at once. The host prices it from the plan: no price is sent. Coming back to `returnUrl` changes nothing: the subscription exists once the provider confirms it. Returns the page's address and what will be charged, in minor units.

returnUrl.description: Where the payer comes back to

email.description: The payer's email. Required unless the caller is a signed-in customer.

offerId.description: Take your continuation offer (subscription.offer.mine): free until its date, then charged. A signed-in customer's own offer only.

holderPersonId.description: Staff only: the Person who holds what it gives (a child whose parent pays), when not the payer. The payer, named by email, is billed; the trial and access are the holder's.

trialDays.description: The free days given; null: charged from the start

freeUntil.description: Free until this moment (a continuation offer taken), then charged; else null

noTrial.description: Why the plan's trial was not given: sign_in (a guest: only a signed-in customer gets a trial), used (one trial per person per plan, had already), permission (staff without subscriptions:manage), held (another page with the trial is open for this person), unconfirmed (the payment provider could not say whether an earlier page was completed; try again later for the trial), continuation (this person has an open continuation offer on this plan, or a subscription from one still running: no trial on top of it). Null otherwise

operations.name: x.content.categories
operations.description: Every category of posts, by name: its id, name and address (slug), for a site's menu or a post's label. Read-only. (Extension tool from Content 0.2.0.)

operations.name: x.courses.buy
operations.description: Start an order for one course or one bundle. A signed-in customer buys as themselves; a guest gives their email address. The host prices it from the record and refuses one outside its sale window. A course the caller already holds access to is refused as one that does not exist. Nothing is paid here: the buyer then calls order.checkout with the order's id (and a guest's token) to pay on the provider's page. Amounts in the minor unit. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

token.description: A guest's key to this order, shown once

operations.name: x.courses.catalogue
operations.description: The published courses, bundles and themes, for a catalogue page: each course's title, theme, level, summary, cover, trailer, price and number of lessons; each bundle's courses and price; the themes in their order. Prices are in the major unit of `currency`. Filter by theme or level. Only what the public may read: a draft is not here. Read-only. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

currency.description: The currency prices are in (ISO 4217), the deployment's one; null until it is set

operations.name: x.courses.course
operations.description: One published course by its address (slug): its fields, its description, its outline's sections and lessons (title, kind, minutes, whether a free preview) and, for a signed-in customer, whether they hold access and which lessons they have done. Not found for a draft or an unknown address. Read-only. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

currency.description: The currency prices are in (ISO 4217), the deployment's one; null until it is set

holds.description: The caller holds access: show open, not buy

done.description: The lesson keys the caller has done

operations.name: x.courses.lesson
operations.description: One lesson of a published course for someone who holds access to it (or any lesson marked a free preview): its kind and its material (a video and notes, a page of text, a training session, a download), where the student left its video, and the next lesson. A video is named with where it is shown: the app asks media.play for a token to play it. Not found without access, as a lesson that does not exist. Read-only. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

lesson.description: The lesson as the outline has it

video.description: Pass to media.play to get a token and the address it plays at

position.description: Seconds: where the student left the video

operations.name: x.courses.myCourses
operations.description: Every course the signed-in student holds access to and why (bought, in a bundle, given by staff, imported, or through their course subscription), with how far they are (lessons done of those that count, complete) and the lesson to continue with. The host says which they hold; nothing here decides it. Read-only. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

continueWith.description: The first lesson not done yet

operations.name: x.courses.plans
operations.description: The course plans on offer: a subscription to every published course, paid every month. Each plan's title, description, price per month (in the major unit of `currency`) and the days of its free trial. Whether a person gets the trial is the host's, when they subscribe (subscription.start): one per person, signed in. Read-only. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

price.description: Per month, in the major unit of `currency`

currency.description: The currency prices are in (ISO 4217), the deployment's one; null until it is set

operations.name: x.courses.progress
operations.description: Mark a lesson started or done, and keep where its video was left (seconds), for the signed-in student. A video watched to within 10 seconds of its end counts as done (give its `duration`). The host refuses it, as a course that does not exist, when the student does not hold access to the course. Returns the lesson's progress and the course's. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

operations.name: x.courses.startSession
operations.description: For a session lesson: the signed-in student's own Programs session for it, once the program is assigned to them (it is, from the day they first open the course: the dates are a suggested pace). operations.name: x.memberships.buy
operations.description: Start an order for one pass (a class pack, a drop-in or an intro offer). operations.name: x.memberships.mine

operations.name: x.ticketing.myTickets
operations.description: The signed-in customer's own tickets: each with its event (id, name, start, end, venue and state, as they are now, whether or not the event is still on sale), its ticket type (id and name), its code and its state (valid, used or void). Only the caller's tickets exist here; a code that is not theirs finds nothing. Filter by event or by code. Read-only. (Extension tool from Ticketing 0.1.0.)

code.description: Only the ticket with this code

timeZone.description: The event's IANA time zone, e.g. Asia/Bangkok: show its start and end, and count its days, in this zone. Null only for an event made before events had one.

eventStatus.description: The event's state now: draft, on_sale, ended or cancelled

operations.name: x.ticketing.orderStart
operations.description: Start an order for tickets: one or more ticket types and how many of each, paid in full or by deposit when every ticket type offers one. A signed-in customer buys as themselves; a guest gives their email address. The host prices the order from the ticket types, refuses a ticket type outside its sale window, over its most per order or without enough places left (with details naming the rule), and holds the places while the order is unpaid. Nothing is paid here: the buyer then calls order.checkout with the order's id (and a guest's token) to pay on the provider's page. Amounts are in the minor unit. (Extension tool from Ticketing 0.1.0.)

email.description: A guest's email address. A signed-in customer passes none.

token.description: A guest's key to this order, shown once (order.checkout and order.view take it)
